16800-the-secret-of-a-happy-home-1896.creator: Unknown
16800-the-secret-of-a-happy-home-1896.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Some one asked me the other day, if I were not "weary of being so often put forward to talk of 'How to Make Home Happy,' a subject upon which nothing new could be said."

77646-oberland.title: Oberland
77646-oberland.creator: Dorothy M. Richardson
77646-oberland.description: A book by Dorothy M. Richardson. emainder of her strength she dropped her things on the platform with a decisiveness she tried just in vain to scorn, and stood still and looked about amongst the hurrying passengers and saw passing by and going ahead to the movement of an English stride the familiar, blessed outlines of a Burberry.

arxiv-2101-00400.title: An Elo-like System for Massive Multiplayer Competitions
arxiv-2101-00400.creator: Aram Ebtekar, Paul Liu
arxiv-2101-00400.description: Abstract . Rating systems play an important role in competitive sports and games. They provide a measure of player skill, which incentivizes competitive performances and enables balanced match-ups. In this paper, we present a novel Bayesian rating system for contests with many participants.

arxiv-2111-11207.title: Improved Sample Complexity Bounds for Branch-and-Cut
arxiv-2111-11207.creator: Maria-Florina Balcan, Siddharth Prasad, Tuomas Sandholm, Ellen Vitercik
arxiv-2111-11207.description: Abstract Branch-and-cut is the most widely used algorithm for solving integer programs, employed by commercial solvers like CPLEX and Gurobi. Branch-and-cut has a wide variety of tunable parameters that have a huge impact on the size of the search tree that it builds, but are challenging to tune by hand.

arxiv-2201-03239.title: There is no rose without a thorn: Finding weaknesses on BlenderBot 2.0’s in terms of Model, Data and User-Centric Approach
arxiv-2201-03239.creator: Jungseob Lee, Midan Shim, Suhyune Son, Chanjun Park, Yujin Kim, Heuiseok Lim
arxiv-2201-03239.description: Abstract BlenderBot 2.0 is a dialogue model that represents open-domain chatbots by reflecting real-time information and remembering user information for an extended period using an internet search module and multi-session. Nonetheless, the model still has room for improvement. To this end, we examine BlenderBot 2.0’s limitations and errors from three perspectives: model, data, and user.

arxiv-2207-08500.title: A six-point neuron-based ENO (NENO6) scheme for compressible fluid dynamics Journal: XXX
arxiv-2207-08500.creator: Yue Li, Lin Fu, Nikolaus A. Adams
arxiv-2207-08500.description: Abstract In this work, we introduce a deep artificial neural network (ANN) that can detect locations of discontinuity and build a six-point ENO-type scheme based on a set of smooth and discontinuous training data. While a set of candidate stencils of incremental width is constructed, the ANN instead of a classical smoothness indicator is deployed for an ENO-like sub-stencil selection.

arxiv-2404-05843.title: Softmax Attention with Constant Cost per Token
arxiv-2404-05843.creator: Franz A. Heinsen
arxiv-2404-05843.description: Abstract We propose a simple modification to the conventional attention mechanism applied by Transformers: Instead of quantifying pairwise query-key similarity with scaled dot-products, we quantify it with the logarithms of scaled dot-products of exponentials. Our modification linearizes attention with exponential kernel feature maps, whose corresponding feature function is infinite dimensional.

arxiv-2409-11164.title: Synthetic data augmentation for robotic mobility aids to support blind and low vision people
arxiv-2409-11164.creator: Hochul Hwang, Krisha Adhikari, Satya Shodhaka, Donghyun Kim
arxiv-2409-11164.description: Abstract Robotic mobility aids for blind and low-vision (BLV) individuals rely heavily on deep learning-based vision models specialized for various navigational tasks. However, the performance of these models is often constrained by the availability and diversity of real-world datasets, which are challenging to collect in sufficient quantities for different tasks.

arxiv-2410-20306.title: Gumbel-NeRF: Representing Unseen Objects as Part-Compositional Neural Radiance Fields
arxiv-2410-20306.creator: Yusuke SekikawaChingwei Hsu †⋆ Satoshi Ikehata † Rei Kawakami †, Ikuro Sato
arxiv-2410-20306.description: Abstract We propose Gumbel-NeRF, a mixture-of-expert (MoE) neural radiance fields (NeRF) model with a hindsight expert selection mechanism for synthesizing novel views of unseen objects. Previous studies have shown that the MoE structure provides high-quality representations of a given large-scale scene consisting of many objects.

arxiv-2411-00936.title: Induced Compton scattering in magnetized electron and positron pair plasma
arxiv-2411-00936.creator: Rei Nishiura, Shoma F. Kamijima, Masanori Iwamoto, Kunihito Ioka
arxiv-2411-00936.description: Abstract A formulation for the parametric instability of electromagnetic (EM) waves in magnetized pair plasma is developed. The linear growth rate of induced Compton scattering is derived analytically for frequencies below the cyclotron frequency for the first time. We identify three modes of density fluctuation: ordinary, charged, and neutral modes .

arxiv-2411-17266.title: Polarization and Orbital Angular Momentum Encoded Quantum Toffoli Gate Enabled by Diffractive Neural Networks
arxiv-2411-17266.creator: Qianke Wang, Dawei Lyu, Jun Liu, Jian Wang
arxiv-2411-17266.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Qianke Wang, Dawei Lyu, Jun Liu, Jian Wang. Controlled quantum gates play a crucial role in enabling quantum universal operations by facilitating interactions between qubits. Direct implementation of three-qubit gates simplifies the design of quantum circuits, thereby being conducive to performing complex quantum algorithms. Here, we propose and present an experimental demonstration of a quantum Toffoli gate fully exploiting the polarization and orbital angular momentum of a single photon.

arxiv-2601-15085.title: The Hadron-Parton Bridge From the QCD Vacuum to Partons
arxiv-2601-15085.description: Abstract Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) exhibits complementary descriptions of hadrons: a rest-frame picture based on confinement, chiral symmetry breaking and interquark forces, and a high-energy light-front picture expressed through parton distributions (PDFs,TMDs,GPDs) and form factors. This review develops a unified framework that connects these two domains. It is based mostly on multiple studies by the authors in the past few years.

pmc-10605881.title: How Toll-like Receptor 9 Plays a Key Role in the Development of Gastric Cancer and Is Linked to Epstein–Barr Virus Infection
pmc-10605881.creator: Marek Majewski, Paulina Mertowska, Sebastian Mertowski, Kamil Torres, Ewelina Grywalska
pmc-10605881.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Simple SummaryTLR-9, a vital component of our immune system, is found to be significantly involved in the progression of gastric cancer. This research also investigates its connection to EBV infection. By analyzing specific T and B immune cell groups that express TLR-9, along with the levels of soluble TLR-9 in the blood, the study compares these factors between individuals with gastric cancer and healthy volunteers.

pmc-10681948.title: Multi-omic analysis characterizes molecular susceptibility of receptors to SARS-CoV-2 spike protein
pmc-10681948.creator: Fanjie Wu, Chenghao Lin, Yutong Han, Dingli Zhou, Kang Chen, Minglei Yang, Qinyuan Xiao, Haiyue Zhang, Weizhong Li
pmc-10681948.description: In the post COVID-19 era, new SARS-CoV-2 variant strains may continue emerging and long COVID is poised to be another public health challenge. Deciphering the molecular susceptibility of receptors to SARS-CoV-2 spike protein is critical for understanding the immune responses in COVID-19 and the rationale of multi-organ injuries. Currently, such systematic exploration remains limited.

pmc-10740665.title: Prediction of Antibody Viscosity from Dilute Solution Measurements
pmc-10740665.creator: Kamal Bhandari, Yangjie Wei, Brendan R Amer, Emma M Pelegri-O’Day, Joon Huh, Jeremy D Schmit
pmc-10740665.description: The high antibody doses required to achieve a therapeutic effect often necessitate high-concentration products that can lead to challenging viscosity issues in production and delivery. Predicting antibody viscosity in early development can play a pivotal role in reducing late-stage development costs. In recent years, numerous efforts have been made to predict antibody viscosity through dilute solution measurements.

pmc-11314492.title: Advance in the Thermoinhibition of Lettuce (Lactuca sativa L.) Seed Germination
pmc-11314492.creator: Jinpeng Wei, Qi Zhang, Yixin Zhang, Le Yang, Zhaoqi Zeng, Yuliang Zhou, Bingxian Chen
pmc-11314492.description: Thermoinhibition refers to the inability of seeds to germinate when inhibited by high temperatures, but when environmental conditions return to normal, the seeds are able to germinate rapidly again, which is different from thermodormancy. Meanwhile, with global warming, the effect of the thermoinhibition phenomenon on the yield and quality of crops in agricultural production is becoming common.

pmc-11479557.title: Can individual functional improvements be predicted in osteoarthritic patients after total knee arthroplasty?
pmc-11479557.creator: Sung Eun Kim, Du Hyun Ro, Myung Chul Lee, Hyuk-Soo Han
pmc-11479557.description: PurposeTotal knee arthroplasty (TKA) is an effective treatment for advanced osteoarthritis, and achieving optimal outcomes can be challenging due to various influencing factors. Previous research has focused on identifying factors that affect postoperative functional outcomes. However, there is a paucity of studies predicting individual postoperative improvement following TKA. Therefore, a quantitative prediction model for individual patient outcomes is necessary.

pmc-11646067.title: P027 Dream characteristics are sex-specific in REM Sleep Behaviour Disorder and healthy older adults
pmc-11646067.creator: S Bramich, A Noyce, L Pérez-Carbonell, A Bindoff, X Wang, A King, S Naismith, J Vickers, J Alty
pmc-11646067.description: IntroductionREM sleep behaviour disorder (RBD) is strongly associated with neurodegenerative disease (NDD), and the isolated form is a known prodrome of several alpha-synuclein-related NDD’s. RBD is difficult to diagnose, and screening questionnaires focus on vivid and aggressive dream content, but these characteristics may be more common to males, leading to underdiagnosis of RBD in females.

pmc-12960054.creator: Koral V. Wheeler, Victoria R. Tennant, Noelle N. Lee, Maxwell W. Hand, Suchita Ganesan, Patrick Walsh, Meral Tubi, Jamie A. Terner, Brandon Hall, Marylan Davison, Arthur W. Toga, Sid O'Bryant, Alexandra L. Clark, Kristine Yaffe, Meredith N. Braskie, Meredith Braskie, Meredith Braskie, Kevin King, Ja
pmc-12960054.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). INTRODUCTIONClarifying relationships between amyloid, tau, and cognition is crucial to understanding dementia risk, but has been mainly performed in non‐Hispanic White (NHW) participants. pmc-13105915.title: Case Report: Giant undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma of the breast combined with contralateral high-grade intraductal carcinoma
pmc-13105915.creator: Zhikun Zhao, Lei Cao, Shengju Xu, Fan Yang, Shang Gao, Chuanxin Ren, Xingchao Xu, Xiangqi Li
pmc-13105915.description: This article reports an exceptionally rare case of a 43-year-old female presenting with concurrent giant pleomorphic undifferentiated sarcoma and high-grade intraductal carcinoma of the contralateral breast. The tumor, remarkably large and comparable in size to a basketball, presented significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges.

pmc-13141528.title: Parity, body mass index, smoking and risk of rheumatoid arthritis: data from the Australian Longitudinal Study on Women’s Health
pmc-13141528.creator: Louise Koller-Smith, Ahmed Mehdi, Syeda Farah Zahir, Lyn March, Leigh Tooth, Gita D Mishra, Ranjeny Thomas
pmc-13141528.description: BackgroundSmoking, obesity and lower parity appear to be associated with higher risk of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in European, American and some Asian studies, but no studies have tested these associations in the Australian context.MethodsWe studied an incident RA cohort of the prospectively collected Australian Longitudinal Study on Women’s Health (ALSWH) dataset.

pmc-13220924.title: The Role of the Digital Workplace in Enhancing Productive Organizational Energy: An Analytical Study at the University of Fallujah
pmc-13220924.creator: Amna Laith Alhashimi, Yasser Lateef Khalaf, Aleksy Kwilinski, Maciej Kardas, Aleksy Kwilinski, Maciej Kardas, amna alhashimi, Silvia Farias-Gaytan, amna alhashimi
pmc-13220924.description: BackgroundDigital workplaces are increasingly adopted in higher education institutions as part of broader digital transformation initiatives. However, many universities still view digital workplace systems primarily as technological tools rather than integrated socio-organizational environments capable of supporting employee engagement and productive organizational energy.

pmc-13349733.title: Response to commentary: “Propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia and recurrence-free survival after hepatectomy-does it improve outcomes?”
pmc-13349733.creator: Ji-Hye Kwon, Jeayoun Kim, Gaab Soo Kim
pmc-13349733.description: y influences cancer recurrence remains unresolved. As they rightly point out, retrospective studies—even large ones—are inherently limited by residual confounding, and the existing randomized controlled trial (RCT) evidence, including our own, has so far not demonstrated a clear survival benefit of propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) over volatile anesthesia in the short term.

pmc-13631009.title: Public knowledge, safety perceptions, and use patterns of ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) among Saudi adults: a mixed-methods study
pmc-13631009.creator: Amal I. Khalil, Aseel F. Aljohani
pmc-13631009.description: Background Withania somnifera, commonly known as ashwagandha, is a widely used herbal remedy with reported anxiolytic and adaptogenic properties. Despite its growing use globally and regionally, comprehensive public understanding of its pharmacological benefits, safety, and potential risks remains limited within the Saudi Arabian context.
